title: Java SQLite Game Library
description: A desktop app for browsing games and managing a personal library
speakerNotes:
- This project is a desktop game library built with Java and SQLite.
- It lets a person browse games and manage a personal collection.
- The interface uses Swing, with JDBC connecting Java to the database.

title: What works now
description: Working features and current app status
speakerNotes:
- The app supports browsing, searching, and filtering by genre.
- Users can manage games and user records, then save games with ratings and play counts.
- The slide also notes that 14 automated tests pass and the Swing window launches in Replit VNC.

title: Project components and tools
description: Desktop UI, database, build, repository, and VNC tools
speakerNotes:
- Swing provides the desktop screens; SQLite and sqlite-jdbc connect the app to its local database.
- DAO classes keep SQL separate from the interface.
- Maven and JUnit 4 support the build and tests; GitHub tracks the source, and Replit VNC displays the desktop window in a browser.

title: Four tables, one game library
description: Four-table relationship diagram and data model
speakerNotes:
- The data is organized into genres, games, users, and user_games.
- A genre can be linked to many games; user_games connects users and games in a many-to-many relationship.
- The user_games table also stores each saved game's rating and play count.

title: What the database answers
description: JOIN, GROUP BY, and aggregate reports
speakerNotes:
- The JOIN combines saved-game records with game and user details to show who saved each game.
- GROUP BY user supports per-user game and play totals.
- The report uses COUNT, SUM, and AVG for games, plays, and ratings; user input is passed with PreparedStatements.

title: Safe input and Java algorithm
description: Input validation, database rules, and insertion sort
speakerNotes:
- The app validates titles, email addresses, web links, and dates in YYYY-MM-DD form.
- Database rules enforce unique names, valid ratings, and non-negative play counts; SQL values use PreparedStatements.
- Java insertion sort orders titles, and tests cover DAO operations, reports, and input validation.

title: Project timeline to Friday
description: Gantt-style schedule from completed work to presentation target
speakerNotes:
- The timeline marks the diagram, schema, seed data, JDBC/DAO, queries, algorithm, and tests as complete.
- The Swing GUI, README, demo guide, and VNC launch are also marked complete for Wed, Nov 4.
- Finishing slides and rehearsing are in progress or planned; Fri, Nov 6 is the classroom presentation target.

title: Five-minute app walkthrough
description: A clear sequence for a classroom demo
speakerNotes:
- Start by searching for a game and filtering by genre, then demonstrate sorting by title.
- Show the JOIN and COUNT/SUM/AVG report, followed by adding, editing, or deleting a temporary record.
- Finish by saving a game to a user's library and explaining user_games; open the Swing workflow before presenting.

title: Reflection: plan, test, explain
description: Reflection, Friday preparation, and a future improvement
speakerNotes:
- The separate games, users, genres, and saved-game details help keep the data organized.
- Project tracking helped identify completed work, next steps, and checks; I am responsible for understanding and explaining the code in my own words.
- Before Friday, rehearse the demo and confirm the app opens in VNC; a future improvement is editing or removing a saved-game entry and testing Swing interactions.
